title: Inference under a known covariance shape
title_html: Inference under a known covariance shape
html:
Let 𝛃Y∼Nn(Xβ,σ2V) with V known and positive definite, r=rank(X)<n. Put 𝛆𝛆SSEV=ε^V⊤V−1ε^V=Y⊤V−1(I−AV)Y,sV2=SSEVn−r.{#eq-ggm-sse}

  1. For 𝛌λ∈C(X⊤), the statistic 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β^V is the same for every solution of the generalized normal equations, and 𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛌λ⊤β^V∼N(λ⊤β, σ2λ⊤(X⊤V−1X)−λ). It is the best linear unbiased estimator of 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β (@cor-opt-aitken).

  2. SSEV/σ2∼χ2(n−r), independently of 𝛃Xβ^V.

  3. E(sV2)=σ2 and Var(sV2)=2σ4/(n−r).

  4. For estimable 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β with 𝛌λ≠0, 𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛌λ⊤β^V−λ⊤βsVλ⊤(X⊤V−1X)−λ∼t(n−r).

  5. Let C(X0)⊆C(X) with rank(X0)=r0<r, and let SSEV,0 be @eq-ggm-sse computed in the reduced model. Then F=(SSEV,0−SSEV)/(r−r0)sV2∼F(r−r0,n−r,γ),{#eq-ggm-f}

    with 𝛃γ=‖(M∗−M∗0)X∗β‖2/σ2, where M∗ and M∗0 are the orthogonal projections onto C(V−1/2X) and C(V−1/2X0). The noncentrality is zero iff 𝛃Xβ∈C(X0).
